questions.q: In the photovoltaic effect, what frees the electrons that make current?
choices: photons of light hitting the silicon junction
why: No — heat actually lowers a cell's output; light does the work.
Correct! Photons free electrons across the silicon p–n junction, driving DC.
No — the inverter comes after; it converts DC the cell already made.

questions.q: A home uses 6 kWh/day with ~5 peak-sun hours. Roughly how much panel power is needed?
why: No — that is too small; recheck 6 kWh ÷ 5 h.
Correct! 6 kWh ÷ 5 h ≈ 1.2 kW (about three 400 W panels, plus losses).
No — that is far oversized for a 6 kWh/day home.
